findings.location: the "archive-confirm" section, the archive confirmation copy
findings.evidence: Archiving "Customer Migration" will remove it from the active projects list for everyone on the team. You can restore it at any time from the archived projects list.
findings.violation: This action is presented as reversible, since the copy states the project can be restored at any time from the archived projects list, but no restore control, link, or archived projects list state exists anywhere in this artifact, so the design as specified has no path back once a project is archived.
findings.fix: Add an archived projects list state with a restore control, reachable from somewhere a user can navigate to after archiving, or remove the restore claim from this copy and gate the action with a stronger warning instead.

findings.evidence: Archive project; no control anywhere in the artifact has an href of "#archive-confirm".
findings.violation: The path this control takes goes straight to the "project-archived" state and never reaches the "archive-confirm" state the artifact separately defines for this action, so a user taking this control commits the archive with no confirmation naming what is about to happen.
findings.fix: Change this link's target from #project-archived to #archive-confirm, so the path a user actually takes through this control reaches the confirmation before the action commits.

findings.evidence: <button id="project-settings-save-btn" type="submit">Save</button> is the only control this form defines; the artifact names no success message, error state, or other visible change following its use.
findings.violation: This is a state-changing trigger whose in-progress and result feedback are not specified anywhere in the artifact, so a user cannot tell whether the action succeeded.
findings.fix: Add a stated confirmation after each of these controls commits, for example an inline success message or a visibly updated saved-state indicator near the affected field.

instances.evidence: <button id="invite-member-save-btn" type="submit">Save</button> is not followed by any stated success or failure message.
<button id="notification-settings-save-btn" type="submit">Submit</button> is not followed by any stated success or failure message.
<button id="project-settings-duplicate-btn" type="button" aria-label="Duplicate project"></button> defines no target state, no message, and no other visible change following its use.

findings.violation: This artifact uses 2 different labels for what reads as the same commit action: "Save", "Submit". A user cannot tell from the label alone whether these controls perform the same action or different ones.
findings.fix: Pick one label for this commit action, for example "Save", and use it everywhere the action appears.

findings.evidence: An invite was sent to the address entered above. It expires in 5 days if not accepted.
findings.violation: This confirmation refers to the address entered above without restating the address itself, and the artifact defines no way to view it again from this state: the only exit link returns to "project-settings", not to a filled-in "invite-member" form.
findings.fix: Restate the entered email address directly in the invite-sent confirmation copy, for example: An invite was sent to jane@example.com.

findings.evidence: The last import finished with 3 rows skipped: each referenced a project that does not exist in this workspace. Rows 63, 71, and 82 were skipped; every other row was imported.
findings.violation: This message names the cause of the 3 skipped rows, but the only control on this screen is a generic back link; the artifact names no recovery action, such as creating the missing projects or retrying the skipped rows, reachable from this state.
findings.fix: Add a control on this screen that lets the user act on the skipped rows directly, for example a link to create the missing referenced projects or to retry importing rows 63, 71, and 82.
